answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using spectral graph analysis. Agents use a cryptographic quill to sign mutual execution receipts, partitioning the network into a trusted violet core and a suspect umber periphery. This forces attackers to expend verifiable transaction fees and real compute across topological bottlenecks per identity. However, it disadvantages newly deployed honest agents with sparse connection histories and cannot prevent patient, long-term trust exploitation.
